explanation: They also sang of peace on earth. “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men on whom His favor rests!” (Luke 2:14, BSB)

content: After the angels left, what did the shepherds find when they hurried to Bethlehem?
options: The Baby lying in the manger
explanation: It was just as the angel had said. “So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph and the Baby, who was lying in the manger.” (Luke 2:16, BSB)

content: How old was Jesus when He stayed behind in Jerusalem after the Passover?
explanation: His family went up for the feast every year. “And when He was twelve years old” (Luke 2:42, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: After the Passover feast, who stayed behind in Jerusalem without His parents knowing?
explanation: His parents thought He was with the group. “the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.” (Luke 2:43, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: After how many days did Mary and Joseph find the twelve-year-old Jesus?
explanation: They searched anxiously. “Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts” (Luke 2:46, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: Where did Mary and Joseph find the twelve-year-old Jesus?
options: In the temple with the teachers
explanation: He was listening and asking questions. “they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers” (Luke 2:46, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: How did people in the temple react to the twelve-year-old Jesus?
explanation: His answers astonished them. “And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.” (Luke 2:47, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: As young Jesus grew up, He grew in wisdom and stature and in favor with whom?
explanation: He grew up in Nazareth. “And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.” (Luke 2:52, BSB)
tags: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

content: By the Lake of Gennesaret, whose boat did Jesus sit in to teach the crowd?
explanation: He asked Simon to push out a little from shore. “Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon” (Luke 5:3, BSB)

content: After teaching from Simon's boat, what did Jesus tell Simon to do?
options: Let down nets in deep water
explanation: Simon obeyed even though he was tired. “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.” (Luke 5:4, BSB)

content: Before Jesus told him to fish again, how had Simon's night of fishing gone?
explanation: They had worked hard all night. “we have worked hard all night without catching anything.” (Luke 5:5, BSB)

content: When Simon let down his nets as Jesus said, what happened?
options: So many fish the nets tore
explanation: Both boats were filled. “they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.” (Luke 5:6, BSB)

content: After the huge catch of fish, what did Simon Peter say about himself?
explanation: He fell at Jesus' knees. “for I am a sinful man.” (Luke 5:8, BSB)

content: After the huge catch, Jesus told Simon that from now on he would catch what?
explanation: Simon would bring people to God. “From now on you will catch men.” (Luke 5:10, BSB)

content: After the miraculous catch, what did the fishermen leave to follow Jesus?
explanation: Following Jesus mattered most. “they left everything and followed Him.” (Luke 5:11, BSB)

content: Which question led Jesus to tell the story of the Good Samaritan?
explanation: An expert in the law asked it. “And who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29, BSB)

content: In the Good Samaritan story, what happened to the man going down to Jericho?
options: Robbers beat him and left him
explanation: He was left half dead. “when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.” (Luke 10:30, BSB)

content: In the Good Samaritan story, what did the priest do when he saw the hurt man?
options: Passed by on the other side
explanation: He did not stop to help. “but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story, who stopped and had compassion on the hurt man by the road?
explanation: The one people least expected showed love. “But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.” (Luke 10:33, BSB)

content: In the Good Samaritan story, what did the Samaritan pour on the man's wounds?
explanation: He bandaged the wounds himself. “and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine.” (Luke 10:34, BSB)

content: Where did the Good Samaritan take the hurt man?
explanation: He put him on his own animal. “brought him to an inn, and took care of him.” (Luke 10:34, BSB)

content: At the end of the Good Samaritan story, what did Jesus tell the expert in the law?
explanation: Being a neighbor means showing mercy. “Go and do likewise.” (Luke 10:37, BSB)

content: Which woman welcomed Jesus into her home in a village?
explanation: Her sister Mary lived there too. “a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.” (Luke 10:38, BSB)

content: While Jesus visited Martha's home, what did her sister Mary do?
explanation: She wanted to hear His message. “who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.” (Luke 10:39, BSB)

content: Why was Martha upset when Jesus visited her home?
options: Mary left her to serve alone
explanation: She was busy with all the preparations. “do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?” (Luke 10:40, BSB)

content: Jesus told Martha she was worried and upset about what?
explanation: Only one thing was really needed. “you are worried and upset about many things.” (Luke 10:41, BSB)

content: When Martha complained, Jesus said Mary had chosen what?
explanation: Listening to Jesus would not be taken from her. “Mary has chosen the good portion” (Luke 10:42, BSB)

content: What was the name of Martha's sister who sat listening to Jesus?
explanation: She chose to listen. “She had a sister named Mary” (Luke 10:39, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the man have?
explanation: He lost just one. “if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them” (Luke 15:4, BSB)

content: In the parable of the lost sheep, what does the shepherd leave to look for the lost one?
explanation: Every single sheep matters to him. “does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost” (Luke 15:4, BSB)

content: In the parable of the lost sheep, how does the shepherd carry the sheep home?
explanation: He carries it joyfully. “he joyfully puts it on his shoulders” (Luke 15:5, BSB)

content: In the parable of the lost sheep, what does the shepherd tell his friends when he gets home?
explanation: He found what was lost. “Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!” (Luke 15:6, BSB)

content: In the parable of the lost sheep, heaven rejoices over one sinner who does what?
explanation: God loves to find the lost. “there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents” (Luke 15:7, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the prodigal son, what did the younger son ask his father for?
explanation: He wanted his inheritance early. “Father, give me my share of the estate.” (Luke 15:12, BSB)

content: In the parable of the prodigal son, how did the younger son waste his money?
explanation: He went to a distant country. “where he squandered his wealth in wild living.” (Luke 15:13, BSB)

content: After spending all his money, what job did the prodigal son have to take?
explanation: A severe famine came. “who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.” (Luke 15:15, BSB)

content: When the father saw his lost son coming home, what did he do?
options: Ran to him and kissed him
explanation: He was filled with compassion. “He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.” (Luke 15:20, BSB)

content: What did the father put on his son who came home?
options: The best robe, a ring, sandals
explanation: He welcomed him back as a son. “Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.” (Luke 15:22, BSB)

content: To celebrate his son's return, what did the father have killed for the feast?
explanation: It was time to celebrate. “Bring the fattened calf and kill it.” (Luke 15:23, BSB)

content: How did the older brother react to the party for his returning brother?
explanation: He refused to go in. “The older son became angry and refused to go in.” (Luke 15:28, BSB)

content: What was Zacchaeus's job?
explanation: He was very wealthy. “a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.” (Luke 19:2, BSB)

content: Why couldn't Zacchaeus see Jesus over the crowd?
explanation: He was small in stature. “because he was small in stature.” (Luke 19:3, BSB)

content: What did Zacchaeus climb so he could see Jesus?
explanation: Jesus was about to pass that way. “So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him” (Luke 19:4, BSB)

content: What did Jesus say when He saw Zacchaeus up in the tree?
options: Hurry down, I'll stay at your house
explanation: Jesus wanted to be his guest. “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.” (Luke 19:5, BSB)

content: Why did people grumble when Jesus went to Zacchaeus's house?
explanation: Jesus came for sinners. “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!” (Luke 19:7, BSB)

content: After meeting Jesus, how much of his possessions did Zacchaeus give to the poor?
explanation: Meeting Jesus changed him. “half of my possessions I give to the poor” (Luke 19:8, BSB)

content: After meeting Zacchaeus, Jesus said He came to seek and save whom?
explanation: That is why He came. “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” (Luke 19:10, BSB)

content: Which two disciples did Jesus send to prepare the Passover meal?
explanation: It would be His last supper with them. “Jesus sent Peter and John” (Luke 22:8, BSB)

content: At the Last Supper, what did Jesus say He had eagerly desired?
options: To eat this Passover with them
explanation: His suffering was near. “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.” (Luke 22:15, BSB)

content: At the Last Supper, what did Jesus say about the bread He broke?
options: This is My body, given for you
explanation: He would give His body on the cross. “This is My body, given for you” (Luke 22:19, BSB)

content: At the Last Supper, Jesus told His disciples to do this in remembrance of whom?
explanation: The Lord's Supper remembers Him. “do this in remembrance of Me.” (Luke 22:19, BSB)

content: At the Last Supper, what did Jesus call the cup?
options: The new covenant in My blood
explanation: His blood was poured out for them. “This cup is the new covenant in My blood” (Luke 22:20, BSB)

content: Jesus told Peter he would deny Him how many times before the rooster crowed?
explanation: It happened just as Jesus said. “the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.” (Luke 22:34, BSB)

content: After Jesus was taken to the high priest's house, where did Peter sit?
options: By a fire in the courtyard
explanation: He followed at a distance. “When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.” (Luke 22:55, BSB)

content: In the high priest's courtyard, who first said Peter had been with Jesus?
explanation: She saw him in the firelight. “A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight” (Luke 22:56, BSB)

content: When the servant girl said Peter was with Jesus, what did Peter say?
options: Woman, I do not know Him
explanation: Peter was afraid. ““Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.” (Luke 22:57, BSB)

content: What happened while Peter was still denying Jesus the third time?
explanation: Jesus' words came true. “While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.” (Luke 22:60, BSB)

content: When the rooster crowed after Peter's denial, what did Jesus do?
explanation: Peter remembered Jesus' words. “And the Lord turned and looked at Peter.” (Luke 22:61, BSB)

content: After denying Jesus three times, what did Peter do?
explanation: He was heartbroken. “And he went outside and wept bitterly.” (Luke 22:62, BSB)

content: What was the place called where Jesus was crucified?
explanation: Criminals were crucified beside Him. “When they came to the place called The Skull” (Luke 23:33, BSB)

content: On the cross, what did Jesus pray for the people crucifying Him?
explanation: They did not know what they were doing. “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” (Luke 23:34, BSB)

content: On the cross, what did Jesus promise the criminal who asked to be remembered?
options: You will see Me in Galilee
explanation: Jesus forgave him. “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.” (Luke 23:43, BSB)

content: In Luke, what did Jesus call out just before He breathed His last?
options: Into Your hands I commit My Spirit
explanation: He gave His life to the Father. “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” (Luke 23:46, BSB)

content: When the women came to Jesus' tomb early Sunday morning, what did they find?
explanation: Jesus was not there. “They found the stone rolled away from the tomb” (Luke 24:2, BSB)

content: At the empty tomb, what did the two men in shining clothes ask the women?
options: Why look for the living among the dead?
explanation: Jesus was alive. “Why do you look for the living among the dead?” (Luke 24:5, BSB)

content: When Peter ran to Jesus' tomb, what did he see inside?
explanation: He went away wondering. “And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths” (Luke 24:12, BSB)

content: On the day Jesus rose, which village were two of His followers walking to?
explanation: They talked about all that had happened. “That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus” (Luke 24:13, BSB)

content: On the road to Emmaus, who came up and walked with the two disciples?
explanation: They did not know it was Him. “Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.” (Luke 24:15, BSB)

content: Why didn't the two disciples on the road to Emmaus recognize Jesus?
options: Their eyes were kept from it
explanation: God kept them from knowing Him yet. “But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.” (Luke 24:16, BSB)

content: What was the name of one of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus?
explanation: He thought the stranger had not heard the news. “One of them, named Cleopas” (Luke 24:18, BSB)

content: At Emmaus, when did the two disciples recognize Jesus?
explanation: Then He disappeared from their sight. “and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.” (Luke 24:35, BSB)

content: Remembering their walk to Emmaus, how did the two disciples say their hearts had felt?
explanation: Jesus had opened the Scriptures to them. “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road” (Luke 24:32, BSB)

content: After recognizing Jesus at Emmaus, where did the two disciples go right away?
explanation: They had to tell the others. “And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.” (Luke 24:33, BSB)

content: In Luke, who was the priest whose wife Elizabeth had no children?
explanation: They were both old and righteous. “there was a priest named Zechariah” (Luke 1:5, BSB)

content: What name did the angel tell Zechariah to give his son?
explanation: He would become John the Baptist. “and you are to give him the name John.” (Luke 1:13, BSB)

content: Because Zechariah did not believe the angel's message, what happened to him?
explanation: He stayed silent until the promise came true. “And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass” (Luke 1:20, BSB)

content: The angel told Mary which relative of hers was also expecting a son in her old age?
explanation: She was in her sixth month. “Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age” (Luke 1:36, BSB)

content: How does Mary's song of praise in Luke begin?
options: Glory to God in the highest
explanation: She rejoiced in God her Savior. “My soul magnifies the Lord” (Luke 1:46, BSB)

content: Which Roman ruler ordered the census that brought Joseph to Bethlehem?
explanation: Everyone had to register in his own town. “a decree went out from Caesar Augustus” (Luke 2:1, BSB)

content: What did the angel tell the shepherds was born in the city of David?
explanation: It was news for all people. “Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!” (Luke 2:11, BSB)

content: After the shepherds' visit, what did Mary do with all these things?
explanation: She thought deeply about them. “But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.” (Luke 2:19, BSB)

content: For which feast did Jesus' parents go to Jerusalem every year?
explanation: They went when Jesus was twelve too. “Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.” (Luke 2:41, BSB)

content: By which lake was Jesus standing when He called Simon to follow Him?
explanation: It is another name for the Sea of Galilee. “while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret” (Luke 5:1, BSB)

content: Who were Simon's fishing partners, the sons of Zebedee?
explanation: They were amazed at the catch too. “and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee.” (Luke 5:10, BSB)

content: What did the expert in the law ask Jesus just before the Good Samaritan story?
options: Why He healed on the Sabbath
explanation: He wanted to test Jesus. “what must I do to inherit eternal life?” (Luke 10:25, BSB)

content: In the Good Samaritan story, who was the second man to pass by the hurt traveler?
explanation: He also passed by on the other side. “So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:32, BSB)

content: After the Good Samaritan story, who did the expert say had been a neighbor to the hurt man?
explanation: A neighbor is anyone who shows mercy. “The one who showed him mercy” (Luke 10:37, BSB)

content: In the parable of the prodigal son, what did the hungry son long to eat?
explanation: No one gave him anything. “He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating” (Luke 15:16, BSB)

content: In the parable of the prodigal son, why did the father say they should celebrate?
options: He was lost and is found
explanation: His son was dead and is alive again. “He was lost and is found!” (Luke 15:24, BSB)

content: Zacchaeus promised to repay anyone he had cheated how many times over?
explanation: His life was changed by Jesus. “and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.” (Luke 19:8, BSB)

content: After Zacchaeus changed his ways, what did Jesus say had come to his house?
explanation: Zacchaeus was a son of Abraham too. “Today salvation has come to this house” (Luke 19:9, BSB)

content: In the high priest's courtyard, why did a man insist Peter must have been with Jesus?
options: He wore a robe like Jesus
explanation: Peter denied it a third time. “for he too is a Galilean.” (Luke 22:59, BSB)

content: What did the criminal on the cross ask of Jesus?
explanation: Jesus promised him Paradise. “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!” (Luke 23:42, BSB)

content: In Luke, what happened to the sun and the temple veil when Jesus was dying?
explanation: Creation itself responded. “The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.” (Luke 23:45, BSB)

content: In Luke, what did the two men at the empty tomb tell the women about Jesus?
options: He is not here; He has risen!
explanation: Jesus had told them He would rise. “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6, BSB)

content: When the women told the apostles Jesus had risen, how did the apostles respond?
explanation: It sounded like nonsense to them. “and they did not believe the women.” (Luke 24:11, BSB)

content: At Emmaus, what did the two disciples urge the stranger to do?
explanation: It was nearly evening. “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening” (Luke 24:29, BSB)

content: On the road to Emmaus, where did Jesus begin explaining the Scriptures about Himself?
options: With Moses and all the Prophets
explanation: The whole Old Testament points to Him. “And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.” (Luke 24:27, BSB)

content: At the end of Luke, what happened while Jesus was blessing His disciples?
options: He was carried up into heaven
explanation: This was His ascension. “While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.” (Luke 24:51, BSB)

content: To which priestly division did Zechariah, John the Baptist's father, belong?
explanation: His wife Elizabeth was a daughter of Aaron. “who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah” (Luke 1:5, BSB)

content: In which month of Elizabeth's pregnancy was the angel Gabriel sent to Mary?
explanation: John was about six months older than Jesus. “In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel” (Luke 1:26, BSB)

content: Who was governor of Syria during the census when Jesus was born?
explanation: It was the first census under him. “while Quirinius was governor of Syria.” (Luke 2:2, BSB)

content: The angel Gabriel told Zechariah that he stands in the presence of whom?
explanation: He was sent with good news. “I stand in the presence of God” (Luke 1:19, BSB)

content: How far had Jesus' parents traveled before they noticed the boy was missing?
explanation: They thought He was with relatives. “they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him” (Luke 2:44, BSB)

content: After His parents found Him in the temple, to which town did the boy Jesus return?
explanation: He was obedient to His parents. “Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them.” (Luke 2:51, BSB)

content: How much money did the Good Samaritan give the innkeeper?
explanation: He promised to pay any extra costs. “The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper.” (Luke 10:35, BSB)

content: In the Good Samaritan story, the traveler was going from Jerusalem to which city?
explanation: It was a dangerous road. “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho” (Luke 10:30, BSB)

content: In the prodigal son parable, what did the older brother say his father never gave him?
explanation: He felt his loyalty was ignored. “Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.” (Luke 15:29, BSB)

content: In which city did Jesus meet Zacchaeus?
explanation: Jesus was passing through. “Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.” (Luke 19:1, BSB)

content: In Luke, on which day was the Passover lamb to be sacrificed?
explanation: Jesus then sent Peter and John to prepare. “Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.” (Luke 22:7, BSB)

content: In Luke, about which hour did darkness come over the land at the crucifixion?
explanation: It lasted until the ninth hour. “It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.” (Luke 23:44, BSB)

content: Which women named in Luke told the apostles about the empty tomb?
explanation: Other women were with them too. “It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James” (Luke 24:10, BSB)

content: About how far was the village of Emmaus from Jerusalem?
explanation: The two disciples walked it on Easter day. “about seven miles from Jerusalem.” (Luke 24:13, BSB)

content: At the end of Luke, as far as which village did Jesus lead His disciples before He was taken up?
explanation: There He lifted up His hands and blessed them. “When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany” (Luke 24:50, BSB)

content: In Capernaum, how many men carried the paralyzed man to Jesus?
explanation: His friends carried him on a mat. “Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.” (Mark 2:3, BSB)

content: Why did the paralyzed man's friends open up the roof of the house?
explanation: The house was packed with people. “Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him” (Mark 2:4, BSB)

content: How did the friends get the paralyzed man to Jesus in the crowded house?
explanation: Nothing stopped them from bringing their friend to Jesus. “made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.” (Mark 2:4, BSB)

content: When Jesus saw the friends' faith, what did He first say to the paralyzed man?
explanation: Jesus cared about his heart first. “Son, your sins are forgiven.” (Mark 2:5, BSB)

content: When Jesus forgave the paralyzed man, who did the scribes say alone can forgive sins?
explanation: Jesus showed He has God's authority. “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” (Mark 2:7, BSB)

content: What did Jesus tell the healed paralyzed man to pick up and take home?
explanation: The man walked out in front of everyone. “get up, pick up your mat, and go home.” (Mark 2:11, BSB)

content: After the paralyzed man walked out healed, what did the amazed crowd say?
explanation: They glorified God. “We have never seen anything like this!” (Mark 2:12, BSB)

content: When Jesus and His disciples crossed the sea one evening, what came up?
explanation: Waves broke over the boat. “Soon a violent windstorm came up” (Mark 4:37, BSB)

content: During the storm on the sea, what was Jesus doing in the boat?
explanation: He was not afraid of the storm. “But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion.” (Mark 4:38, BSB)

content: When the disciples woke Jesus in the storm, what did they ask Him?
options: Don't You care we are perishing?
explanation: They were terrified. “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?” (Mark 4:38, BSB)

content: In the storm, what did Jesus say to the wind and the sea?
explanation: Even the weather obeys Him. ““Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!”” (Mark 4:39, BSB)

content: After Jesus rebuked the wind on the sea, what happened?
explanation: The storm stopped at His word. “And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.” (Mark 4:39, BSB)

content: After calming the storm, what did Jesus ask His disciples?
explanation: He wanted them to have faith. ““Why are you so afraid?” He asked.” (Mark 4:40, BSB)

content: After Jesus stopped the storm, what did the disciples ask one another?
options: Who is this that the wind obeys?
explanation: They were amazed at His power. “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?” (Mark 4:41, BSB)

content: What was Jairus, the man who fell at Jesus' feet and begged for help?
explanation: He came for his sick daughter. “A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived” (Mark 5:22, BSB)

content: Why did Jairus beg Jesus to come to his house?
explanation: He believed Jesus could heal her. “My little daughter is near death.” (Mark 5:23, BSB)

content: While Jesus was on the way to Jairus's house, what news arrived?
explanation: The messengers thought it was too late. “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?” (Mark 5:35, BSB)

content: When Jairus heard his daughter had died, what did Jesus tell him?
options: Do not be afraid; just believe
explanation: Jesus was about to do the impossible. “Do not be afraid; just believe.” (Mark 5:36, BSB)

content: At Jairus's house, what did Jesus say about the girl?
options: She is not dead, but asleep
explanation: For Jesus, death was like sleep. “The child is not dead, but asleep.” (Mark 5:39, BSB)

content: When Jesus said Jairus's daughter was only asleep, how did the mourners react?
explanation: They knew she had died. “And they laughed at Him.” (Mark 5:40, BSB)

content: How old was Jairus's daughter when Jesus raised her?
explanation: She got up and walked around. “She was twelve years old” (Mark 5:42, BSB)

content: After raising Jairus's daughter, what did Jesus tell them to give her?
explanation: She was truly alive and hungry. “and He told them to give her something to eat.” (Mark 5:43, BSB)

content: As Jesus was leaving which city did He meet blind Bartimaeus by the road?
explanation: Bartimaeus sat by the road begging. “as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho” (Mark 10:46, BSB)

content: What did blind Bartimaeus cry out when he heard Jesus passing by?
options: Son of David, have mercy on me!
explanation: He believed Jesus was the promised King. ““Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”” (Mark 10:47, BSB)

content: When people told blind Bartimaeus to be quiet, what did he do?
explanation: He would not give up. “but he cried out all the louder” (Mark 10:48, BSB)

content: When Jesus called him, what did blind Bartimaeus throw off?
explanation: He jumped up and came to Jesus. “Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.” (Mark 10:50, BSB)

content: When Jesus asked what he wanted, what did blind Bartimaeus ask for?
explanation: He asked for what only Jesus could give. “let me see again.” (Mark 10:51, BSB)

content: What did Jesus say had healed blind Bartimaeus?
explanation: He trusted Jesus. “your faith has healed you.” (Mark 10:52, BSB)

content: After he could see, what did Bartimaeus do?
explanation: He became a follower of Jesus. “And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.” (Mark 10:52, BSB)

content: When people brought little children to Jesus, what did the disciples do?
explanation: They thought Jesus was too busy. “and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.” (Mark 10:13, BSB)

content: How did Jesus feel when the disciples turned the children away?
explanation: Children matter to Jesus. “But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant” (Mark 10:14, BSB)

content: What did Jesus tell His disciples about the little children?
explanation: He told them not to stop the children. “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them!” (Mark 10:14, BSB)

content: When the children came to Him, Jesus said the kingdom of God belongs to whom?
explanation: God welcomes those who come like children. “For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” (Mark 10:14, BSB)

content: Blessing the children, Jesus said we must receive God's kingdom like what?
explanation: With simple trust. “anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.” (Mark 10:15, BSB)

content: What did Jesus do with the children who were brought to Him?
explanation: He placed His hands on them. “And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.” (Mark 10:16, BSB)

content: How does the Gospel of Mark open?
options: In the days of King Herod
In the beginning was the Word
A record of the family line
explanation: Mark calls Jesus the Son of God from the start. “This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” (Mark 1:1, BSB)

content: In Mark, what did Jesus do early in the morning while it was still dark?
options: Went to a solitary place to pray
explanation: Jesus made time to be alone with God. “Jesus got up and slipped out to a solitary place to pray.” (Mark 1:35, BSB)

content: In the region of the Gerasenes, what did the man with the unclean spirit say his name was?
explanation: He said, “for we are many.” ““My name is Legion,” he replied” (Mark 5:9, BSB)

content: When Jesus cast the spirits out of the man called Legion, where did they go?
explanation: The herd rushed into the sea. “the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs” (Mark 5:13, BSB)

content: How long had the woman who touched Jesus' cloak suffered from bleeding?
explanation: Doctors had not helped her. “And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.” (Mark 5:25, BSB)

content: What did the sick woman in the crowd believe would heal her?
explanation: Her bleeding stopped at once. “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.” (Mark 5:28, BSB)

content: What did Jesus tell the woman who was healed by touching His cloak?
explanation: He called her “Daughter.” ““Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” (Mark 5:34, BSB)

content: In Jesus' hometown, what work did people say He did?
explanation: They took offense at Him. “Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary” (Mark 6:3, BSB)

content: When Jesus sent out the Twelve, how did He send them?
explanation: He gave them authority over unclean spirits. “and began to send them out two by two” (Mark 6:7, BSB)

content: When Jesus healed a deaf man, which Aramaic word did He say?
explanation: It means, “Be opened!” ““Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).” (Mark 7:34, BSB)

content: After Jesus first touched the blind man at Bethsaida, what did people look like to him?
explanation: Jesus touched his eyes again and he saw clearly. “but they look like trees walking around.” (Mark 8:24, BSB)

content: Jesus asked what it profits a man to gain the whole world, yet lose what?
explanation: The soul is worth more than the world. “What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?” (Mark 8:36, BSB)

content: What did the father of the troubled boy cry out to Jesus?
options: I do believe; help my unbelief!
explanation: Jesus had said all things are possible for one who believes. “I do believe; help my unbelief!” (Mark 9:24, BSB)

content: Jesus said whoever wants to be first must be what?
options: Last of all and servant of all
explanation: Greatness in God's kingdom means serving. “he must be the last of all and the servant of all.” (Mark 9:35, BSB)

content: What did Jesus tell the rich young man to do with everything he owned?
options: Sell it and give to the poor
explanation: Then he would have treasure in heaven. “Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor” (Mark 10:21, BSB)

content: Why did the rich young man go away sad after talking with Jesus?
explanation: He loved his riches too much. “because he had great wealth.” (Mark 10:22, BSB)

content: Jesus said the Son of Man came not to be served, but to do what?
options: To serve and give His life
explanation: He gave His life as a ransom for many. “For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.” (Mark 10:45, BSB)

content: What did the poor widow put into the temple treasury?
explanation: Jesus was watching the givers. “Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins” (Mark 12:42, BSB)

content: Why did Jesus say the poor widow gave more than all the others?
explanation: The others gave out of their extra. “but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.” (Mark 12:44, BSB)

content: Who was forced to carry the cross of Jesus?
explanation: He was passing by from the country. “Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by” (Mark 15:21, BSB)

content: On the way to Jesus' tomb, what were the women worried about?
options: Who would roll away the stone
explanation: The stone was very large, but it was already rolled away. “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?” (Mark 16:3, BSB)

content: In Mark, where did the risen Jesus tell His disciples to go and preach the gospel?
explanation: The gospel is for every creature. “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.” (Mark 16:15, BSB)

content: In which town was the house where the paralyzed man was lowered through the roof?
explanation: Jesus had come back home there. “A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum.” (Mark 2:1, BSB)

content: During the storm on the sea, in which part of the boat was Jesus sleeping?
explanation: He slept on a cushion. “But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion.” (Mark 4:38, BSB)

content: When Jesus met the man called Legion, which region had He sailed to?
explanation: It was on the other side of the sea. “they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.” (Mark 5:1, BSB)

content: About how many pigs rushed into the sea when the unclean spirits entered them?
explanation: The herd drowned in the water. “and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea” (Mark 5:13, BSB)

content: What words did Jesus say when He took Jairus's daughter by the hand?
explanation: It means, “Little girl, get up!” “Jesus said, “Talitha koum!”” (Mark 5:41, BSB)

content: Which disciples did Jesus allow to go with Him to Jairus's house?
explanation: He let no one else come along. “except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.” (Mark 5:37, BSB)

content: Blind Bartimaeus was the son of whom?
explanation: Bar-timaeus means son of Timaeus. “a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus” (Mark 10:46, BSB)

content: What title did blind Bartimaeus use when he asked Jesus to heal him?
explanation: It means my teacher. ““Rabboni,” said the blind man” (Mark 10:51, BSB)

content: In Bethany, in whose home did a woman pour perfume on Jesus' head?
explanation: Jesus was reclining at the table there. “in the home of Simon the Leper” (Mark 14:3, BSB)

content: What was the expensive perfume poured on Jesus' head in Bethany made of?
explanation: It came in an alabaster jar. “a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard.” (Mark 14:3, BSB)

content: Simon of Cyrene, who carried Jesus' cross, was the father of whom?
explanation: Mark's readers may have known his sons. “the father of Alexander and Rufus” (Mark 15:21, BSB)

content: According to Mark, at what hour was Jesus crucified?
explanation: That is about nine in the morning. “It was the third hour when they crucified Him.” (Mark 15:25, BSB)

content: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem, who came from the east to find Him?
explanation: They came looking for the newborn King of the Jews. “Magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem” (Matthew 2:1, BSB)

content: What did the Magi see in the east that led them to look for the newborn King?
explanation: They came to worship Him. “We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him.” (Matthew 2:2, BSB)

content: What gifts did the Magi give the Child Jesus?
explanation: They fell down and worshiped Him. “gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.” (Matthew 2:11, BSB)

content: After the Magi left, where did an angel tell Joseph to flee with baby Jesus?
explanation: King Herod wanted to kill the Child. “Take the Child and His mother and flee to Egypt.” (Matthew 2:13, BSB)

content: What did John the Baptist preach in the wilderness of Judea?
explanation: He prepared the way for Jesus. “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.” (Matthew 3:2, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: What did John the Baptist eat in the wilderness?
explanation: He lived a simple life in the desert. “His food was locusts and wild honey.” (Matthew 3:4, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: What were John the Baptist's clothes made of?
explanation: He wore a leather belt too. “John wore a garment of camel’s hair” (Matthew 3:4, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: In which river did John the Baptist baptize the people?
explanation: People came confessing their sins. “they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.” (Matthew 3:6, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: When Jesus was baptized, what came down on Him like a dove?
explanation: The heavens opened as He came out of the water. “He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.” (Matthew 3:16, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: After John baptized Jesus in the Jordan, what did God's voice from heaven say?
explanation: God the Father was well pleased with Jesus. “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!” (Matthew 3:17, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: When Jesus came to be baptized, what did John the Baptist first say?
options: I need to be baptized by You
explanation: John knew Jesus was greater than he. “I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?” (Matthew 3:14, BSB)
tags: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus

content: Where was Jesus led by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil?
explanation: This happened right after His baptism. “Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.” (Matthew 4:1, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before He was tempted?
explanation: Afterward He was hungry. “After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.” (Matthew 4:2, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: In the wilderness, what did the devil tell hungry Jesus to turn stones into?
explanation: Jesus answered with God's word. “tell these stones to become bread.” (Matthew 4:3, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: Tempted in the wilderness, Jesus said man shall not live on bread alone, but on what?
explanation: God's word is real food for the soul. “but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.” (Matthew 4:4, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: When tempting Jesus, where did the devil set Him and tell Him to jump?
explanation: Jesus would not test God. “and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.” (Matthew 4:5, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: From a very high mountain, what did the devil show Jesus to tempt Him?
options: All the kingdoms of the world
explanation: He offered them if Jesus would worship him. “showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.” (Matthew 4:8, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: After the devil left Jesus in the wilderness, who came and served Him?
explanation: Jesus had defeated every temptation. “Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.” (Matthew 4:11, BSB)
tags: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness

content: In the Beatitudes, who will see God?
explanation: Jesus taught this in the Sermon on the Mount. “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.” (Matthew 5:8, BSB)

content: In the Beatitudes, who will be called sons of God?
explanation: God's children make peace. “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.” (Matthew 5:9, BSB)

content: In the Beatitudes, what will the meek inherit?
explanation: Gentle people are blessed. “Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.” (Matthew 5:5, BSB)

content: In the Beatitudes, what does Jesus promise to those who mourn?
explanation: God comforts the sad. “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.” (Matthew 5:4, BSB)

content: In the Beatitudes, who will be shown mercy?
explanation: Those who show mercy receive mercy. “Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.” (Matthew 5:7, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus calls His followers the salt of what?
explanation: Salt gives flavor and keeps food from spoiling. “You are the salt of the earth.” (Matthew 5:13, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus calls His followers the light of what?
explanation: A city on a hill cannot be hidden. “You are the light of the world.” (Matthew 5:14, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said people do not put a lamp under what?
explanation: A lamp is meant to give light to everyone. “Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket.” (Matthew 5:15, BSB)

content: How does the Lord's Prayer begin?
explanation: Jesus taught us to pray to God as Father. “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.” (Matthew 6:9, BSB)

content: In the Lord's Prayer, where do we ask for God's will to be done as it is in heaven?
explanation: We pray for God's kingdom to come. “Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” (Matthew 6:10, BSB)

content: In the Lord's Prayer, what do we ask God to give us this day?
explanation: We trust God for what we need each day. “Give us this day our daily bread.” (Matthew 6:11, BSB)

content: In the Lord's Prayer, we ask God to forgive our debts as we have done what?
explanation: Forgiven people forgive others. “And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.” (Matthew 6:12, BSB)

content: In the Lord's Prayer, from whom do we ask God to deliver us?
explanation: We also ask not to be led into temptation. “but deliver us from the evil one.” (Matthew 6:13, BSB)

content: In the Lord's Prayer, what do we say about God's name?
explanation: Hallowed means honored as holy. “hallowed be Your name.” (Matthew 6:9, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, where did the wise man build his house?
explanation: A strong foundation keeps the house standing. “is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.” (Matthew 7:24, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, where did the foolish man build his house?
explanation: Sand cannot hold a house in a storm. “is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.” (Matthew 7:26, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, why did the wise man's house stand through the storm?
options: Its foundation was on the rock
explanation: Obeying Jesus is like building on rock. “yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.” (Matthew 7:25, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, what happened to the house on sand?
options: It fell with a great crash
explanation: Hearing without doing leads to ruin. “and it fell—and great was its collapse!” (Matthew 7:27, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, the wise man is like someone who hears Jesus' words and does what?
explanation: Doing what Jesus says is wise. “everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man” (Matthew 7:24, BSB)

content: In Jesus' story of two builders, what beat against the house on the rock?
explanation: Storms come to everyone. “The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house” (Matthew 7:25, BSB)

content: How did Jesus come to His disciples' boat in the middle of the night?
explanation: He has power over the sea. “Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.” (Matthew 14:25, BSB)

content: When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea, what did they think He was?
explanation: They cried out in fear. ““It’s a ghost!” they said” (Matthew 14:26, BSB)

content: Walking on the water, what did Jesus tell His frightened disciples?
explanation: He told them not to be afraid. “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.” (Matthew 14:27, BSB)

content: Which disciple got out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus?
explanation: Jesus told him, “Come.” “Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.” (Matthew 14:29, BSB)

content: Why did Peter begin to sink while walking on the water?
options: He saw the wind and was afraid
explanation: He took his eyes off Jesus. “But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid” (Matthew 14:30, BSB)

content: As Peter began to sink in the sea, what did he cry out?
explanation: Jesus reached out and caught him. “cried out, “Lord, save me!”” (Matthew 14:30, BSB)

content: After Jesus walked on the water and the wind stopped, what did the disciples say?
options: Truly You are the Son of God
explanation: They worshiped Him in the boat. “Truly You are the Son of God!” (Matthew 14:33, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the sower, what ate the seed that fell on the path?
explanation: The seed never had a chance to grow. “some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.” (Matthew 13:4, BSB)

content: In the parable of the sower, why did the seedlings on rocky ground wither?
explanation: The soil was too shallow. “and they withered because they had no root.” (Matthew 13:6, BSB)

content: In the parable of the sower, what happened to the seed that fell among thorns?
explanation: The thorns grew up around it. “Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.” (Matthew 13:7, BSB)

content: In the parable of the sower, what did the seed on good soil do?
explanation: Good soil is like a heart that receives God's word. “Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop” (Matthew 13:8, BSB)

content: Explaining the sower, Jesus said the good soil is someone who hears the word and does what?
explanation: God's word grows in a ready heart. “But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit” (Matthew 13:23, BSB)

content: Explaining the sower, what did Jesus say the thorns stand for?
explanation: They choke God's word in our hearts. “but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word” (Matthew 13:22, BSB)

content: Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is like which tiny seed?
explanation: Small beginnings can grow very large. “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.” (Matthew 13:31, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable, what does the tiny mustard seed grow into?
explanation: It becomes the largest of garden plants. “and becomes a tree” (Matthew 13:32, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the mustard seed, who comes to nest in its branches?
explanation: The kingdom grows big enough to shelter many. “so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.” (Matthew 13:32, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable, how does the mustard seed compare with other seeds?
explanation: Yet it grows into something great. “Although it is the smallest of all seeds” (Matthew 13:32, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the ten virgins, whom did they go out to meet?
explanation: They took their lamps to meet him. “took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.” (Matthew 25:1, BSB)

content: In the parable of the ten virgins, how many of them were wise?
explanation: The other five were foolish. “Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.” (Matthew 25:2, BSB)

content: In the parable of the ten virgins, what did the wise ones bring with their lamps?
explanation: They were ready for a long wait. “But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.” (Matthew 25:4, BSB)

content: In the parable of the ten virgins, what happened when the bridegroom was late?
explanation: All ten became drowsy. “they all became drowsy and fell asleep.” (Matthew 25:5, BSB)

content: In the parable of the ten virgins, when did the cry ring out that the bridegroom was coming?
explanation: He came when they did not expect. “At midnight the cry rang out” (Matthew 25:6, BSB)

content: In the parable of the ten virgins, what happened after the ready ones went in to the feast?
explanation: The foolish ones were too late. “and the door was shut.” (Matthew 25:10, BSB)

content: What lesson did Jesus give at the end of the parable of the ten virgins?
explanation: No one knows the day or the hour. “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.” (Matthew 25:13, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable of the talents, how many talents did the first servant receive?
explanation: Each got an amount based on his ability. “To one he gave five talents” (Matthew 25:15, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, what did the servant with one talent do with it?
explanation: He did nothing with what he was given. “dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.” (Matthew 25:18, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, what did the master say to the servants who gained more?
options: Well done, good and faithful servant
explanation: Faithfulness with a little brings more. “Well done, good and faithful servant!” (Matthew 25:21, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, how many more talents did the five-talent servant gain?
explanation: He put the money to work at once. “went at once and put them to work and gained five more.” (Matthew 25:16, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, why did the one-talent servant say he hid the money?
explanation: Fear kept him from using what he had. “So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground.” (Matthew 25:25, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, who received the talent taken from the fearful servant?
explanation: Those who use what they have are given more. “Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.” (Matthew 25:28, BSB)

content: Before entering Jerusalem, what animals did Jesus send two disciples to bring?
explanation: The King came humbly on a donkey. “you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her.” (Matthew 21:2, BSB)

content: As Jesus rode into Jerusalem, what did the crowd spread on the road?
explanation: They welcomed Him like a king. “A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees” (Matthew 21:8, BSB)

content: As Jesus rode into Jerusalem, what did the crowds shout?
options: Hosanna to the Son of David!
explanation: They praised Him as the promised King. “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9, BSB)

content: After entering Jerusalem, whose tables did Jesus overturn in the temple courts?
explanation: They had turned God's house into a market. “He overturned the tables of the money changers” (Matthew 21:12, BSB)

content: When Jesus cleared the temple, He said His house should be called a house of what?
explanation: They had made it a den of robbers. “My house will be called a house of prayer.” (Matthew 21:13, BSB)

content: On which mount was Bethphage, where Jesus stopped before entering Jerusalem?
explanation: From there He sent two disciples ahead. “came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives” (Matthew 21:1, BSB)

content: Where did Jesus go to pray with His disciples on the night He was arrested?
explanation: He prayed there before the cross. “Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane” (Matthew 26:36, BSB)

content: In Gethsemane, Jesus prayed, “Yet not as I will, but…” what?
explanation: Jesus obeyed His Father completely. “Yet not as I will, but as You will.” (Matthew 26:39, BSB)

content: When Jesus came back from praying in Gethsemane, what were His disciples doing?
explanation: They could not keep watch for one hour. “Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping.” (Matthew 26:40, BSB)

content: In Gethsemane, Jesus said the spirit is willing, but what is weak?
explanation: He told them to watch and pray. “For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” (Matthew 26:41, BSB)

content: In Gethsemane, how did Judas show the crowd which one was Jesus?
explanation: It was the signal he had arranged. “Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.” (Matthew 26:49, BSB)

content: In Gethsemane, what was the crowd that came with Judas carrying?
explanation: The chief priests had sent them. “accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs” (Matthew 26:47, BSB)

content: In Gethsemane, which disciples did Jesus take farther with Him?
explanation: He was deeply sorrowful. “He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee” (Matthew 26:37, BSB)

content: In the Great Commission, Jesus told His followers to make disciples of whom?
explanation: The good news is for the whole world. “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19, BSB)

content: In the Great Commission, in whose name are new disciples baptized?
explanation: One God in three persons. “baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19, BSB)

content: In the Great Commission, how long did Jesus promise to be with His disciples?
options: To the end of the age
explanation: Jesus is always with His people. “And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” (Matthew 28:20, BSB)

content: Before giving the Great Commission, what did Jesus say had been given to Him?
options: All authority in heaven and earth
explanation: His command comes with full authority. “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” (Matthew 28:18, BSB)

content: In the Great Commission, what were the disciples to teach new believers?
explanation: Disciples learn to live Jesus' way. “and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you.” (Matthew 28:20, BSB)

content: Matthew says the virgin's son would be called Immanuel. What does Immanuel mean?
explanation: Jesus is God come to be with His people. “(which means, “God with us”).” (Matthew 1:23, BSB)

content: When Jesus called Peter and Andrew by the Sea of Galilee, what did He say He would make them?
explanation: They would bring people to Jesus. “and I will make you fishers of men.” (Matthew 4:19, BSB)

content: When Jesus called Peter and Andrew, what did they leave behind right away?
explanation: They followed Him at once. “And at once they left their nets and followed Him.” (Matthew 4:20, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus tell us to do for our enemies?
options: Love them and pray for them
explanation: God's love reaches even enemies. “love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you” (Matthew 5:44, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said where your treasure is, there your what will be also?
explanation: What we value shows what we love. “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” (Matthew 6:21, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said you cannot serve both God and what?
explanation: No one can serve two masters. “You cannot serve both God and money.” (Matthew 6:24, BSB)

content: Teaching about worry, which creatures did Jesus point to as fed by God without sowing or reaping?
explanation: We are worth much more to God than birds. “Look at the birds of the air” (Matthew 6:26, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus say to seek first?
explanation: Then all these things will be added. “But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness” (Matthew 6:33, BSB)

content: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said not to worry about what?
explanation: Each day has enough trouble of its own. “Therefore do not worry about tomorrow” (Matthew 6:34, BSB)

content: Jesus said ask and it will be given, seek and you will find, and knock and what?
explanation: God answers those who seek Him. “knock, and the door will be opened to you.” (Matthew 7:7, BSB)

content: What did Jesus say is the essence of the Law and the Prophets?
explanation: This is often called the Golden Rule. “In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you.” (Matthew 7:12, BSB)

content: Where was Matthew sitting when Jesus called him to follow?
explanation: Matthew got up and followed Jesus. “He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth.” (Matthew 9:9, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable, the kingdom of heaven is like what hidden in a field?
explanation: The man sold everything to buy the field. “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field.” (Matthew 13:44, BSB)

content: In Jesus' parable, what did the merchant sell everything he had to buy?
explanation: God's kingdom is worth everything. “When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it.” (Matthew 13:46, BSB)

content: Before Jesus fed the five thousand, what food did the disciples have?
explanation: It was not nearly enough for the crowd. “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish” (Matthew 14:17, BSB)

content: After Jesus fed the five thousand, how many baskets of leftovers were picked up?
explanation: Everyone ate and was satisfied. “the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.” (Matthew 14:20, BSB)

content: When Jesus asked, “Who do you say I am?”, what did Peter answer?
options: The Christ, Son of the living God
explanation: God the Father had shown this to Peter. “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” (Matthew 16:16, BSB)

content: When Jesus was transfigured on the mountain, what did His face shine like?
explanation: His clothes became white as light. “His face shone like the sun” (Matthew 17:2, BSB)

content: When Peter asked if he should forgive his brother seven times, what did Jesus answer?
explanation: Forgiveness should have no limit. “not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!” (Matthew 18:22, BSB)

content: Jesus said it is easier for a camel to go through what than for a rich man to enter God's kingdom?
explanation: Riches can keep people from God. “it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle” (Matthew 19:24, BSB)

content: What did Jesus call the first and greatest commandment?
options: Love God with all your heart
explanation: Love God with all your heart, soul, and mind. “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.” (Matthew 22:37, BSB)

content: What did Jesus say is the second commandment, like the first?
explanation: Love for God shows in love for people. “Love your neighbor as yourself.” (Matthew 22:39, BSB)

content: How much did the chief priests pay Judas to hand Jesus over?
explanation: Judas betrayed Jesus for money. “And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.” (Matthew 26:15, BSB)

content: At the Last Supper, what did Jesus say as He gave the disciples the broken bread?
options: Take and eat; this is My body
explanation: His body would be given for them. “Take and eat; this is My body.” (Matthew 26:26, BSB)

content: After denying Jesus three times, what did Peter do when the rooster crowed?
explanation: He remembered what Jesus had said. “And he went outside and wept bitterly.” (Matthew 26:75, BSB)

content: Before handing Jesus over to be crucified, what did Pilate do in front of the crowd?
explanation: He said he was innocent of this man's blood. “he took water and washed his hands before the crowd.” (Matthew 27:24, BSB)

content: When Jesus died on the cross, what happened to the veil of the temple?
explanation: It tore from top to bottom. “At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.” (Matthew 27:51, BSB)

content: After the earthquake at the cross, what did the centurion guarding Jesus say?
options: Truly this was the Son of God
explanation: Even a Roman soldier saw who Jesus was. “Truly this was the Son of God.” (Matthew 27:54, BSB)

content: Where did Joseph of Arimathea place the body of Jesus?
explanation: He rolled a great stone across the entrance. “and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock.” (Matthew 27:60, BSB)

content: At the empty tomb, what did the angel tell the women about Jesus?
options: He is not here; He has risen
explanation: Jesus rose just as He said. “He is not here; He has risen, just as He said!” (Matthew 28:6, BSB)

content: On the morning Jesus rose, who rolled away the stone from the tomb?
explanation: There was a great earthquake. “for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.” (Matthew 28:2, BSB)

content: John the Baptist said he was not worthy to carry what of the One coming after him?
explanation: John knew Jesus was far greater. “whose sandals I am not worthy to carry.” (Matthew 3:11, BSB)

content: John the Baptist said the One after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit and with what?
explanation: John baptized only with water. “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.” (Matthew 3:11, BSB)

content: When the devil told Jesus to jump from the temple, what Scripture did Jesus answer with?
options: Do not put God to the test
Man shall not live on bread
explanation: Jesus would not force God to prove Himself. “Do not put the Lord your God to the test.” (Matthew 4:7, BSB)

content: In Matthew's list of the twelve apostles, what is Matthew called?
explanation: He had worked at a tax booth. “Thomas and Matthew the tax collector” (Matthew 10:3, BSB)

content: In Matthew's list of the twelve apostles, which other Simon is named besides Peter?
explanation: He is listed near Judas Iscariot. “Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot” (Matthew 10:4, BSB)

content: In the parable of the sower, what yields did the seed on good soil produce?
explanation: Good soil bears a rich harvest. “a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.” (Matthew 13:8, BSB)

content: During which watch of the night did Jesus walk on the sea to His disciples?
explanation: It was in the early morning darkness. “During the fourth watch of the night” (Matthew 14:25, BSB)

content: About how many men were fed with five loaves and two fish, besides women and children?
explanation: Women and children ate too. “About five thousand men were fed” (Matthew 14:21, BSB)

content: When Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, what full name did Jesus call him?
explanation: Jesus said the Father had revealed this to him. “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah!” (Matthew 16:17, BSB)

content: Which three disciples went up the high mountain where Jesus was transfigured?
explanation: They saw Jesus' glory. “Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James” (Matthew 17:1, BSB)

content: Clearing the temple, besides the money changers' tables, whose seats did Jesus overturn?
explanation: He drove out all who were buying and selling. “and the seats of those selling doves.” (Matthew 21:12, BSB)

content: In the parable of the talents, how many talents did the second servant receive?
explanation: He gained two more. “to another two talents” (Matthew 25:15, BSB)

content: At the crucifixion, darkness covered the land from which hour to which hour?
explanation: Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice. “From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.” (Matthew 27:45, BSB)

content: In Matthew, what did Jesus cry out in a loud voice about the ninth hour on the cross?
explanation: It means, My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me? ““Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?”” (Matthew 27:46, BSB)

content: Joseph, the rich disciple who buried Jesus, came from which town?
explanation: He asked Pilate for Jesus' body. “there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph” (Matthew 27:57, BSB)

content: At Jesus' tomb, what did the angel's clothes look like?
explanation: His appearance was like lightning. “and his clothes were white as snow.” (Matthew 28:3, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he can do all things through whom?
explanation: His strength came from Jesus. “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” (Philippians 4:13, BSB)

content: In Philippians, what did Paul say he had learned to be in every circumstance?
explanation: He trusted God in plenty and in need. “for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.” (Philippians 4:11, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he knows how to live humbly and also how to do what?
explanation: He was ready for any situation. “I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound.” (Philippians 4:12, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says, “Rejoice in the Lord…”
explanation: He said it twice. “Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!” (Philippians 4:4, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says to be anxious for nothing, but in everything to do what?
explanation: Pray with thanksgiving. “Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.” (Philippians 4:6, BSB)

content: In Philippians, what does Paul say will guard our hearts and minds?
explanation: It surpasses all understanding. “And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds” (Philippians 4:7, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says God will supply all your what?
explanation: According to His glorious riches. “And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:19, BSB)

content: In Philippians, complete Paul's words: “For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is…”
explanation: Death would bring him to Christ. “For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.” (Philippians 1:21, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul is confident God will carry the good work He began in you to what?
explanation: God finishes what He starts. “that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion” (Philippians 1:6, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says in humility to consider others as what?
explanation: Do nothing from selfish pride. “but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.” (Philippians 2:3, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says Christ emptied Himself, taking the form of what?
explanation: He was made in human likeness. “but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant” (Philippians 2:7, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says Christ humbled Himself and was obedient to what?
explanation: That is how far His humility went. “He humbled Himself and became obedient to death— even death on a cross.” (Philippians 2:8, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says at the name of Jesus every what should bow?
explanation: God gave Him the highest name. “that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow” (Philippians 2:10, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says do everything without complaining or what?
explanation: Shine like stars in the world. “Do everything without complaining or arguing” (Philippians 2:14, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he presses on toward the goal to win what?
explanation: He forgets what lies behind. “I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 3:14, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says our citizenship is where?
explanation: We await a Savior from there. “But our citizenship is in heaven” (Philippians 3:20, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul lists true, pure, lovely things and says to do what with them?
explanation: Fill your mind with good things. “think on these things.” (Philippians 4:8, BSB)

content: Who joined Paul in greeting the saints at Philippi in his letter?
explanation: Both were servants of Christ. “Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, To all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi” (Philippians 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says he was from which tribe of Israel?
explanation: He was a Hebrew of Hebrews. “of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews” (Philippians 3:5, BSB)

content: In Philippians, which two women did Paul urge to agree in the Lord?
explanation: Unity matters in the church. “I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.” (Philippians 4:2, BSB)

content: In Philippians, whom did Paul call his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier?
explanation: He carried gifts to Paul. “Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier” (Philippians 2:25, BSB)

content: In Philippians, believers from whose household sent special greetings?
explanation: The gospel reached the palace. “especially those from the household of Caesar.” (Philippians 4:22, BSB)

content: In Philippians, Paul says who learned he was in chains for Christ?
explanation: His chains spread the gospel. “it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.” (Philippians 1:13, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to trust in the LORD with how much of your heart?
explanation: God wants our full trust. “Trust in the LORD with all your heart” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells us not to lean on what?
explanation: Our own understanding is limited. “and lean not on your own understanding” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says if you acknowledge God in all your ways, He will do what?
explanation: God guides those who trust Him. “and He will make your paths straight.” (Proverbs 3:6, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs warns us not to be wise in whose eyes?
explanation: Instead, fear the LORD and turn from evil. “Be not wise in your own eyes” (Proverbs 3:7, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says to honor the LORD with your wealth and with what?
explanation: God deserves our first and best. “Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest” (Proverbs 3:9, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says the LORD disciplines whom?
explanation: Like a father who delights in his son. “for the LORD disciplines the one He loves” (Proverbs 3:12, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells a son not to reject what from the LORD?
explanation: God's correction is a sign of His love. “My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD” (Proverbs 3:11, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says a true friend loves when?
explanation: Real friends stay through hard times. “A friend loves at all times” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what kind of answer turns away anger?
explanation: Kind words calm people down. “A gentle answer turns away wrath” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs tells the lazy person to learn from which creature?
explanation: The ant works hard without being told. “Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker” (Proverbs 6:6, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what goes before destruction?
explanation: A haughty spirit comes before a fall. “Pride goes before destruction” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a child trained in the way he should go will do what when he is old?
explanation: Good training lasts a lifetime. “Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.” (Proverbs 22:6, BSB)

content: In its opening chapter, Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Fools despise wisdom and discipline. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” (Proverbs 1:7, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to guard what with all diligence, because springs of life flow from it?
explanation: What is in the heart shapes all of life. “Guard your heart with all diligence” (Proverbs 4:23, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what is detestable to the LORD?
explanation: Those who deal faithfully are His delight. “Lying lips are detestable to the LORD” (Proverbs 12:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to commit what to the LORD so that your plans succeed?
explanation: Then your plans will be achieved. “Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.” (Proverbs 16:3, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a joyful heart is good what?
explanation: A broken spirit dries up the bones. “A joyful heart is good medicine” (Proverbs 17:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs calls the name of the LORD a strong what?
explanation: The righteous run to it for safety. “The name of the LORD is a strong tower” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens whom?
explanation: Friends help each other grow. “As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.” (Proverbs 27:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says every word of God is what?
explanation: He is a shield to those who trust Him. “Every word of God is flawless” (Proverbs 30:5, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wife of noble character is far more precious than what?
explanation: Her worth is beyond price. “She is far more precious than rubies.” (Proverbs 31:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but who is to be praised?
options: A woman who fears the LORD
explanation: Character matters more than looks. “but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.” (Proverbs 31:30, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Knowing the Holy One is understanding. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom” (Proverbs 9:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wise son brings joy to whom?
explanation: A foolish son brings grief to his mother. “A wise son brings joy to his father” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a brother is born for what?
explanation: Family helps in hard times. “and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a harsh word does what?
explanation: A gentle answer turns away wrath. “but a harsh word stirs up anger.” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a haughty spirit comes before what?
explanation: Pride goes before destruction. “and a haughty spirit before a fall.” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of what?
explanation: The right word at the right time is beautiful. “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.” (Proverbs 25:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs compares a fool repeating his folly to what?
options: A dog returning to its vomit
explanation: Fools keep making the same mistakes. “As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.” (Proverbs 26:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which small creatures make their homes in the rocks?
explanation: They are weak but wise. “the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks” (Proverbs 30:26, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creatures have no king, yet advance in formation?
explanation: They work together without a ruler. “the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation” (Proverbs 30:27, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creature can be caught in the hand, yet is found in kings' palaces?
explanation: Small things can go far. “and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.” (Proverbs 30:28, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the ants, though weak, do what in the summer?
explanation: They plan ahead. “yet they store up their food in the summer” (Proverbs 30:25, BSB)

content: Whose proverbs begin the section that says a wise son brings joy to his father?
explanation: Solomon wrote many proverbs. “The proverbs of Solomon” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the righteous run to the name of the LORD and are what?
explanation: His name is a strong tower. “the righteous run to it and are safe.” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Complete the start of David's famous psalm: “The LORD is my…”
explanation: God cares for His people like a shepherd. “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” (Psalm 23:1, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, where does the LORD make him lie down?
explanation: The Shepherd gives rest. “He makes me lie down in green pastures” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, beside what does the LORD lead him?
explanation: The Shepherd leads to peaceful places. “He leads me beside quiet waters.” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what does the LORD restore?
explanation: God refreshes us from the inside. “He restores my soul” (Psalm 23:3, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, why does he fear no evil in the dark valley?
explanation: God's presence takes away fear. “I will fear no evil, for You are with me” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, which two things comfort him?
explanation: A shepherd uses them to guide and protect. “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what will follow him all the days of his life?
explanation: He will dwell in the house of the LORD forever. “Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life” (Psalm 23:6, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what happens to his cup?
explanation: God blesses him more than enough. “my cup overflows.” (Psalm 23:5, BSB)

content: In the very first psalm, what does the blessed man delight in?
explanation: He loves God's word. “But his delight is in the Law of the LORD” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, when does the blessed man meditate on God's law?
explanation: God's word fills his thoughts. “and on His law he meditates day and night.” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, the blessed man is like what?
explanation: He grows strong and bears fruit. “He is like a tree planted by streams of water” (Psalm 1:3, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what are the wicked like?
explanation: They have nothing that lasts. “For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.” (Psalm 1:4, BSB)
